\[
(x_c, y_c) = \text{Planckian}(T),
\quad
(u, v)_s = (u, v)(x_c, y_c) + \Delta_{uv}\, \hat{n},
\quad
M = \operatorname{Bradford}(W_s \to W_{\text{D65}}),
\qquad
T = 4500\,\text{K},\ \Delta_{uv} = 0 / 1000
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(T\): The color temperature of the light, in kelvin
- \(x_c, y_c\): The chromaticity of a blackbody at T
- \(\Delta_{uv}\): The distance off the blackbody curve, the tint over 1000
- \(\hat{n}\): The unit direction across the curve, toward green

The chromaticity of a blackbody light at temperature T comes from the cubic spline of Kang and colleagues, valid from 1667 K to 25000 K. The tint moves this white by Duv in the CIE 1960 uv diagram, perpendicular to the blackbody curve, toward green for positive values. The direction comes from two nearby temperatures. That white, with luminance 1, is adapted to D65 with the Bradford transform, as in the chromatic adaptation filter, and the matrix is applied in linear light. D65 itself lies a little above the blackbody curve, toward green, so tint 0 at about 6500 K still shifts the image slightly toward green. These choices of scale and direction are PixelNexus's own. Raw converters use similar controls with their own scales.
